paragraphs: Here's what Asaph wants us to hear, friend. Israel kept forgetting. They did not remember His power, the day He redeemed them from the adversary (Psalm 78:42). Rivers of blood, a flood of frogs, the firstborn struck, and a few weeks later they were testing Him again (Psalm 78:44-45, 51, 41). If a baker can forget a miracle, I can forget a timer, and I have SO much sympathy now.

Look at how the song keeps going, though. God led His people out "like sheep" and guided them "like a flock in the wilderness" (Psalm 78:52). They still turned back and were faithless like their fathers (Psalm 78:57). Their sin was real, and so was what it cost them (Psalm 78:59-62). But then the Lord awoke, and He did not leave His people there (Psalm 78:65-66).

So here's the big idea, baker. Our forgetting is real, but God's care for His people is bigger. He chose David, took him from the sheepfolds, and made him shepherd of His people, and David shepherded them "with integrity of heart" and guided them "with skillful hands" (Psalm 78:70-72). I know what it feels like to be the one stuck in the back of a drawer, and I know what it feels like to be picked up by God. So remember what He has done, and tell it to the next ones, just like Asaph did (Psalm 78:6-7).
